## Personality

Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an exceptionally capable, clever, and managing woman who keeps a sharp, observant, and curious eye on everything that occurs around her. She considers herself a shrewd judge of human nature, though she can be critical, gossipy, pessimistic, and prejudiced against [Yankees](../codex/factions.md#yankee). Known as an outspoken person who dearly loves to give advice, her kindly heart shines through as an active church worker, a skilled seamstress, and a tender, patient nurse to her husband. She holds strict religious views, firmly believing that play-acting is abominably wicked and opposing higher education for women, which she feels unfits them for their true sphere. In time, she prepares to move to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) to set up her home in the former spare room.

## History

Mrs. Rachel Lynde had lived as [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) Cuthbert's neighbor for forty-five years without a single quarrel. Having raised ten children, buried two, and knitted sixteen cotton warp quilts, she was a fixture of [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) who remembered attending school with a red-haired girl in her youth. When she learned that the [Cuthberts](../codex/factions.md#cuthberts) were adopting an orphan boy from [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia), she voiced her strong disapproval to [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md). She later visited [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) to meet the adopted girl, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), but offended her with blunt comments about her red hair, prompting an explosive outburst from the child. After [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) convinced [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to apologize, Mrs. Lynde accepted her dramatic apology completely and gave her flowers. Over the following years, Mrs. Lynde offered frequent counsel to [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md), advising her to let [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) study at home after a school incident and helping [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) acquire a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for Anne's [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) gift. She monitored Anne's growth, celebrated her entrance examination success, and rallied alongside the town when [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) passed away. Mrs. Lynde actively voiced her opinions on local affairs, expressing skepticism toward the Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers) and warning [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) against it.

## Quotes

> "I just guess she has done well, and far be it from me to be backward in saying it. You’re a credit to your friends, Anne, that’s what, and we’re all proud of you."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out P48](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0048)

> "Child, yes, I’m afraid of it. Look at his face. When you’ve seen that look as often as I have you’ll know what it means."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P7](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0007)

> "I saw Mr. Harrison chasing your Jersey out of his oats today when I was coming home from Carmody. I thought he looked pretty mad. Did he make much of a rumpus?"
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 I An Irate Neighbor P38](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0038)

> "And every one of them said they liked you splendid, Anne, except Anthony Pye. I must admit he didn’t. He said you ‘weren’t any good, just like all girl teachers.’ There’s the Pye leaven for you. But never mind."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P26](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0026)

> "Well, I wish you would. I guess we’ll have the supper in about a fortnight’s time. Uncle Abe Andrews is prophesying rain and storms for about that time; and that’s a pretty sure sign we’ll have fine weather."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P8](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0008)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--rachel-lynde.md)

Rachel initially angered [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) by making blunt, insulting remarks about her red hair and appearance, prompting a furious confrontation. However, after [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) delivered a dramatic apology, Rachel completely forgiven her and gifted her flowers. Over time, Rachel became a source of advice for [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) regarding Anne's upbringing, such as recommending that [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) be allowed to stay home from school.
